reasoning: Round 2: both round-1 findings are applied (tasks.md 1.1 parametrization plus the spec's Context not observed WHEN, and D5 'Accepted divergence'). Every class is ok, and the design stays observed and traced.

simpler.evidence: Simpler option 1: PR 151's upsert_ruleset in init. D1 rejects it because a first install cannot have observed the context, and it would reverse 'Init writes only the Project remotely'. Simpler option 2: a one-off manual `gh api -X PUT` on this repository with no script. Issue 154's acceptance rejects it (preflight, dry-run, idempotence, read-back), and so do consumers (issue 117). Simpler option 3: also writing classic protection. The person's decision (2) of 2026-09-23 excludes it. The script reuses set_status.run_gh/Gh (set_status.py:27-38) and adds no new abstraction.

map.evidence: The 10 delta scenarios map one-to-one (tasks.md, Scenario → test map): Quality check on a PR -> existing test_quality_executes_a_trusted_driver_against_the_pr_worktree; PR weakens its own driver -> test_publisher_driver_keeps_a_same_head_catcher; Caller absent, Context not observed, Dry-run, No ruleset yet, Live ruleset differs, Rerun, Ambiguous rulesets, Read-back mismatch -> test_activate_protection.py::test_<name>. No scenario is unmapped. Whether each mapped test is sufficient is judged under length.

platform.evidence: design.md Observations cover the behaviours the design rests on. Ruleset list/GET shape and server-added keys: I re-read ruleset 23732345, which matches, and also shows server-added `required_reviewers []`, not owned per D3. Classic protection has strict checks quality/quality and agent-review/agent-review with app_id 15368 (re-read, matches). The check_name filter and app github-actions/15368 were read on the PR 165 head. GraphQL HEAD:path returns Blob/null. A merged PR keeps headRefOid. PUT by id keeping the id, and owned fields surviving a server round-trip: the live ruleset created from PR 151's template holds the template's owned values, and task 5.4's `written: ruleset 23732345` plus the second `unchanged` dry-run observe it on the real write. D4's read-back fails closed otherwise.

replaced.evidence: D5 lists the replaced ruleset context (quality / quality -> agent-process / quality) and what stops proving. Context/D1 list the package-name boundary ruleset/protection from v2-2g-a. D5 'Accepted divergence' now lists that review_gate.py's input REQUIRED_CONTEXTS lacks agent-process / quality. It names the catchers, which are the ruleset merge block on the same head and wait_for_pr waiting for all checks, and the owners, which are the follow-up issue and issue 115. It adds no new check.

catcher.evidence: D5 failure mode (PR edits ci_check.py/quality.yml/the caller's test). Catcher until the follow-up is classic strict quality / quality, app 15368, enforce_admins true (re-read live). It runs reusable-quality.yml's default-branch driver on the same head, and GitHub enforces it at merge. Drift of that classic state is caught by check_branch_protection.py on .githooks/pre-push against REQUIRED_CONTEXTS, pinned by test 1.2. The catcher after the follow-up is agent-review / agent-review, a review not a re-run, accepted by the person on 2026-09-23 (decision 1). Issue 151's never-reporting-context failure is caught by D2's preflight before any write (scenarios Caller absent / Context not observed). An interrupted write is caught by list-then-decide in D3. Every catcher reaches a named delivery step.
